message.body:
Hi,

I'll be cancelling my plan before my next billing date on 10 October. Once it's cancelled, please delete all the personal data you hold on me.

My NHS number is 999 060 4917 if you need it to find my records.

policy.label: Policy P9.1: Privacy requests and marketing preferences
policy.text:
Requests to see, correct or delete personal information, or questions about how it is used, go to the privacy officer. Agents do not handle these themselves. We acknowledge a request within 2 business days. Response times follow the law in each country: United Kingdom (UK GDPR), within one month.

Health and prescription records must be kept for a minimum period set by law, so a deletion request may only be partly possible. The privacy officer explains what we keep and why. Never promise a full deletion.

Marketing. Any agent can take a patient off marketing emails straight away; it takes effect within 2 business days. Service messages about orders, billing and safety continue while the plan is active. Privacy complaints also go to the privacy officer.

policy.label: Policy P6.1: Pausing, cancelling or changing a plan
policy.text:
Pausing. A plan can be paused for 1 to 3 months at a time. Ask at least 3 days before the next billing date for the pause to apply to that order. With less notice, we can still stop the order and refund it if it has not been dispensed. A paused plan can restart early at any time: the first order goes out on the restart date, which becomes the new billing date. Plans are monthly; there is no two-monthly option, but a pause can space orders out.

Cancelling. A plan can be cancelled at any time with no fee. With at least 3 days' notice before the billing date there are no further charges. Orders that have already been dispatched cannot be recalled.

Changing products. Adding, removing or swapping a product needs a clinician's approval. Once approved, the change and any new price apply from the next billing date.

Stop sending. If a patient says to stop sending, stop, or not send anything more, put every order that has not been dispatched on hold straight away, before replying. Then ask whether they want to pause or cancel. The hold stays until the patient confirms. Reply within 1 business day. If the reason is a health concern, the message goes to a clinician (see clinical questions).

policy.label: Policy P3.2: Renewals and follow-up consults
policy.text:
Each prescription covers a set number of monthly repeats. While a patient is on a plan they have a follow-up consult every 3 months, included in the plan price. When the repeats are about to run out, they need a renewal consult. We email a reminder 21 days before the last repeat is used. A renewal can be done at a booked follow-up if it falls before the next billing date.

Patients should book a renewal consult at least 7 days before their next billing date. If the new prescription is not approved by the billing date, we hold the plan charge and the order waits in script pending; we charge once the prescription is approved, so nobody pays for an order that cannot be sent. Renewal consults on an active plan cost nothing extra. A patient whose plan was cancelled for less than 6 months can restart on their existing prescription if it still has repeats; otherwise they need a new consult.

Agents can book and explain renewals. Only a clinician decides whether to renew a prescription and what is prescribed.
